name: The Halo Benders
label: K
lede: Calvin Johnson ran K Records, Doug Martsch fronted Built to Spill, and together they made three albums in which neither singer read the other's lyrics. A drug stop in Utah ended up on television.

eras.title: A side project with a keyboard in it
eras.text: Johnson fronted Beat Happening and ran K from Olympia; Martsch fronted Built to Spill in Boise. Their two singers wrote their parts apart, and the records sound like it.

years.cap: The Halo Benders live in a small club
years.h: The K Records boss and the Built to Spill guitarist start a band
years.p: [[Calvin Johnson|cac7a688-14a8-46c3-8fc8-11cca866677c]] of [[Beat Happening|449e44cb-bcae-4c48-a1af-5d8df0f81456]] and [[Doug Martsch|42c520b5-4992-4aab-9f3f-542addcde686]] of [[Built to Spill|3ac482b8-1494-4071-a0e9-f192f9d2c2b0]] start the Halo Benders in 1994, with Martsch's Built to Spill drummer Ralf Youtz on drums.
years.xp:
AllMusic lists the first line-up as Johnson, Martsch, bassist Wayne Flower (formerly of Treepeople) and Youtz, with producer Steve Fisk adding keyboards. It describes the group as a whimsical side project pairing two of the Northwest's more idiosyncratic indie rockers.

Per the KCSB write-up of the second album, the two singers deliberately did not write lyrics together or respond to each other's words inside a song. Johnson's baritone and Martsch's higher voice share the songs but not the subject.

years.src: Wikipedia: God Don't Make No Junk · Stereogum
yt: Live at the Capitol Theater, Olympia, 1995
years.h: God Don't Make No Junk goes out on K as KLP29
years.p: Ten songs in 33 minutes, recorded at Dub Narcotic in Olympia with [[Steve Fisk|c851ef86-5278-4537-8b51-7ccedb4ae903]] producing. Trouser Press called it "a stack of strange gems".
years.xp:
Wikipedia gives the release date as June 24, 1994. The book Gimme Indie Rock singled out "Canned Oxygen" as a high point for both principals, and Spin later ranked the record among "Rock's 25 Greatest Team-ups".

Stereogum's Backtrack column hears it as a tossed-off record in the best sense, with a playful first half and a bitter second half about getting older and not liking where things are going. The "Canned Oxygen" 7" came out the same year, per Wikipedia.

years.h: "Don't Touch My Bikini" becomes a single on Fire Records
years.p: The British label puts out the song, first heard on God Don't Make No Junk, as a single in 1995.

eras.title: Phil Ek, cleaner sound, a traffic stop
eras.text: Producer Phil Ek takes over from Steve Fisk and the records get tidier. The lyrics stay apart, and the band's best-known story turns out to be a stop on a Utah highway.

years.cap: Poster for the Halo Benders, Love as Laughter and Mocket at the Capitol Theater, Olympia, 1996
years.src: Wikipedia: Don't Tell Me Now · KCSB
years.h: Don't Tell Me Now brings in Phil Ek and a slower tempo
years.p: Recorded at Dub Narcotic in Olympia and released on K as KLP46. The band slows just enough for the sadder songs to fit.
years.xp:
Wikipedia credits Johnson, Martsch, Flower and Youtz, with Ek on organ and extra drums, Fisk on keyboards, Alex Knold on cello and Jen Smith and Beth Rangert on vocals. KCSB calls it tighter and more polished than the debut, with folk, alt-country and power-pop in its eleven songs.

Trouser Press called it wonderful; CMJ called it a generally worthy follow-up to the first record.

q: To some people it's funny, but to us, it was a bummer.
yt: Halo Benders on Real Stories of the Highway Patrol
years.h: Pulled over in Utah with a TV crew in the passenger seat
years.p: The Halo Benders' van gets searched on camera for Real Stories of the Highway Patrol. Martsch later: "To some people it's funny, but to us, it was a bummer."
years.xp:
Exclaim! reports that officers found a one-hitter with a small amount of marijuana. The driver was handcuffed and arrested for possession, and Johnson was cuffed too after a heated exchange with the police. Martsch was also handcuffed but was not in trouble the way the driver was.

Asked about it later, Martsch said: "Oh, it did happen. Yeah. But I don't really want to talk about it." MONSTERFRESH notes the episode became indie-fan lore before it turned up on YouTube.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Rebels Not In · AllMusic
yt: Canned Oxygen with Built to Spill, Columbus, Oct 22, 1998
years.h: The Rebels Not In is the last album, and the glossy one
years.p: Recorded at Dub Narcotic with Ek again and released as KLP81. Pitchfork gave it 8.8 out of 10.
years.xp:
Magnet described it as the playful spirit of early K set against higher-end production. Beat Happening's [[Heather Dunn|d8a3c735-5583-4e7f-99e4-8a8a79d0e18f]] guests on guitar, and Pitchfork later put "Virginia Reel Around the Fountain" at number 188 on its Top 200 Tracks of the 1990s.

It is the third and last studio album from the group.

years.h: "Bury Me" opens on a drum part borrowed from the Wedding Present
years.p: Wikipedia notes the intro nods to the Wedding Present's 1994 song "Yeah Yeah Yeah Yeah Yeah", and Martsch echoes that phrase in the chorus.

eras.title: Two nights in Boise, one in Olympia
eras.text: Built to Spill's touring kept the Halo Benders on hold. They came back twice, each time for a room in a town that mattered to one of them.

years.cap: The Halo Benders onstage, Johnson and Martsch at the front
years.h: Two reunion nights at the Visual Arts Collective, Boise
years.p: The band plays Martsch's hometown with Youtz back on drums and Brett Netson and Stephen Gere in the line-up, per Wikipedia.

years.cap: The Halo Benders at the Capitol Theater, Olympia, November 2010
yt: "Canned Oxygen" at the Capitol Theater, Nov 21, 2010
years.h: A benefit for Friends of Mia at the Capitol Theater, Olympia
years.p: A one-off in Johnson's hometown with Flower on bass. AllMusic dates the group's formal end to 2010.
